A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same research work, renamed from DisRNN to FacRNN. Their main text, equations, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic experiments and analyses of monkey M1 recordings and mouse voltage imaging, including appendix ablations and Poisson-observation results.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds a monkey M1 penalty sweep and quantitative diagnostics of excess latent dimensions.

M1.justification: Equations (1)-(8) generalize the stated external-input parameterization from neuron-space input η to Uη, with D-dimensional inputs and a learnable projection U. The low-rank recurrence, group structure, and partial-correlation objective remain unchanged; renaming DisRNN to FacRNN is not itself a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Lorenz/Thomas synthetic dynamics, the same described eight-direction monkey reaching recordings, and mouse air-puff voltage imaging, including the retained Poisson-observation analysis. The revised monkey citation and additional mouse acquisition details do not establish different dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same comparison methods and model variants. Although SMC disappears from the general methods list, it remains evaluated in the K=4 monkey experiment and Figures 3 and 10.

E3.justification: V2 adds a reported real-data beta-selection procedure using held-out reconstruction log-likelihood and between-group partial correlation, with eight beta values from 1 to 200 in Table 1. Existing main-experiment budgets and configurations are retained; newly specifying L=1 does not establish a change to those experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix A.3.2 adds the monkey M1 beta sensitivity analysis. Appendix A.3.1 extends the existing oversized-group experiment with PCA explained variance and normality diagnostics to examine inactive dimensions. Earlier synthetic ablations, regrouping analyses, rotation tests, and Poisson results remain.

E5.justification: V2 adds normality tests and coordinate-level p-values in Appendix A.3.1 and specifies means and standard deviations across five runs for the new Table 1 experiment. The existing ten-seed synthetic comparisons and pairwise t-test reporting are retained; no increase in their run count is established.

E6.justification: V2 adds PCA variance ratios, normality-test results, a ground-truth synthetic PC estimate near 0.1, and Table 1 results. For example, beta=20 gives reconstruction log-likelihood 379.661 and between-group PC 0.000620. Main reported scores remain unchanged, including K=4 monkey alignment R2 of 0.79±0.01 and mouse reconstruction R2 values of 0.955, 0.922, and 0.955.

T1.justification: Section 2 corrects the affine reparameterization's encoder from (P^-1 B, d) to (P^-1 B, P^-1 d), fixing the transformed bias. The group-independence definition, Jordan-block derivation, and partition-count formula remain unchanged. The new nonlinear-connectivity appendix provides suggestions, not a new proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: group-wise independent latent dynamics, flexible within-group dependence, interpretable sub-connectivities, and improved latent interpretation. The shift from disentanglement to factorization terminology does not materially change these claims.

C2.justification: V2 narrows the external-input limitation from the formulation to the real-world experiments and characterizes SMC as an ancillary comparison with a different inference pipeline. New Appendix A.2 discusses local Jacobian and attribution-based connectivity proxies. The mouse interpretation also explicitly identifies stimulus-locked contralateral barrel/M2 responses.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a public-code repository link and directs readers there for videos. It newly documents L=1, PC estimation using all time points in each sequence, Gaussian synthetic inputs with U=I, and the mouse experiment's 30 Hz whisker stimulation and JEDI-1P sensor. These are additional disclosures, not evidence that existing experimental settings changed.

R1.justification: V2 replaces the monkey-data reference to Ma et al. (2023) with Gallego et al. (2020) and adds Miller et al. (2023), Cognitive model discovery via disentangled RNNs, to the bibliography. Broad positioning relative to ICA, disentangled VAEs, and low-rank RNNs remains stable.

P1.justification: V2 renames the title and model, revises terminology throughout, and makes targeted explanatory edits while retaining the main narrative order and much of the prose. It adds Software and Data, Acknowledgements, Impact Statement, and nonlinear-connectivity sections, and removes the LLM-use disclosure.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column conference layout for the main text and references, with redesigned title/header formatting and extensively resized and reflowed figures. Figure 4 is substantially rearranged and enlarged, and Table 1 is added. The original ten figures are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses limited validation and reproducibility gaps through the real-data beta sweep, quantitative rank diagnostics, explicit code-access information, and clearer implementation details. It also corrects the blanket external-input limitation and improves Figure 4's legibility. These gains leave the main experimental conclusions intact. The added rank analysis remains incompletely specified, including the unnamed normality test, so the evidence supports a modest overall improvement.
